title: Boy hit during police chase dies
article: A seven-year-old boy from Edmonton, critically injured during a car crash involving a speeding police vehicle on Saturday has died, but his grieving family says his spirit will live on through organ donations.
Giovanni Aleman was a passenger in his grandfather's car when it was broadsided by an unmarked police car speeding through an intersection.
The crash split the car in half and it burst into flames, badly burning Giovanni, his six-year-old brother Jonathon and mother Patricia Ramirez. Jonathon is still in critical condition.
Questions have been raised about why the police car was travelling so fast. Edmonton police say it was chasing two other cars speeding through the city.
A fatality inquiry is expected, which police say could be followed by judicial proceedings.

During an emotional news conference Patricia, whose neck is in a brace, choked back sobs as she said the family is hanging on to its faith in God and that her son's organs would be donated "to work for other kids."

The first recipient is believed to be a seven-year-old girl from Manitoba who is recovering this morning from heart transplant surgery. Andrea Froese had the operation in Edmonton Wednesday night, just hours after Giovanni's life support machine was turned off.
